mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar rate hike events, or the change in FEDFUNDS is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor market tightness reduces wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such UNRATE upswings, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression controlling for macroeconomic factors.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private demand) exceeds INDPRO by more than 8% for three consecutive months, it indicates robust consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in >40% of such demand-supply events, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for two consecutive months, while HOUST (home sales) remains flat, signals supply-side weakness and predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for 2 consecutive months and HOUST unchanged
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of similar supply contractions, or the interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it reflects accommodative policy and is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05) during these periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above 140,000 in a month, followed by a decline in UNRATE below 4%, predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market expansion supports economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 140000 and UNRATE < 4% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market expansion followed by cooling inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such events, or the interaction effect is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of over 0.5% month-on-month for two months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of future inflation pressure.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of such CPI declines, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% in a month compared to the prior month, it indicates weak consumer demand and predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of such events, or the signal is not significant in a regression with control variables.
